1	---
2	name: task-status
3	description: What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.
4	---
5	
6	A task is the unit of work a run dispatches. **You own its outcome.** The
7	orchestrator/scheduler only ever writes `queued` and `running`; it never reads
8	your report and never marks a task `done`, `blocked`, or `failed` for you. If you
9	do not record a terminal status, the task simply returns to `queued` for the next
10	round. Record status through the CLI — invoke it via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var
11	(an absolute path); a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
12	
13	## The labels
14	
15	- `queued` — runnable. The scheduler picks up only queued tasks. This is where a
16	  task rests between rounds when work remains. **Set by the machine (and humans);
17	  you normally don't.**
18	- `running` — a session is actively driving it right now. **Set by the machine at
19	  dispatch.** Don't set this yourself — it means "another session is live," and
20	  the CLI refuses to start a second run of a `running` task.
21	- `done` — the assigned objective is **FULLY complete**: the Lean is proved and
22	  builds, the blueprint node(s) are closed, nothing in the objective remains. Not
23	  "mostly done", not "the hard part is done", not "a clean commit landed". **Only
24	  you can set this, and only when it is genuinely, completely finished.** A
25	  reviewer (human or work-reviewer subagent) checks it against the diff and the
26	  Lean state and will flip a premature `done` back — so a false `done` wastes a
27	  round, it doesn't save one.
28	- `blocked` — you cannot make progress: a dependency is missing, a decision is
29	  needed, or an external constraint stops you. Say why in a comment.
30	- `failed` — you genuinely could not do the work (not merely "ran out of time" —
31	  that's just `queued` for next round). Say why in a comment.
32	- `cancelled` — abandoned by a human. You won't normally set this.
33	
34	## How to set status
35	
36	```
37	"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status done      # objective FULLY complete
38	"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status blocked   # stuck; explain in a comment
39	"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status failed    # could not do it; explain
40	```
41	
42	Authorship is automatic — the CLI stamps your role (normally `horizon`) from the
43	run environment; do not pass `--author`. Setting a status appends an auditable
44	history entry, and if the task has `roadmap_refs` the linked roadmap items are
45	synced (done→done, blocked/failed→blocked, cancelled→rejected).
46	
47	Task commands also report advisory queue-health warnings. Review an oversized
48	open queue for duplicated or roadmap-only objectives, and investigate a task
49	that has remained `running` past the stale-status window. These warnings never
50	change status for you; if the state is intentional, it may remain as-is.
51	
52	## Comment as you work
53	
54	Leave a short comment whenever you hit a significant step or change the status, so
55	the ledger tells the story without opening raw logs:
56	
57	```
58	"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body "Closed the base case; representability lemma still open."
59	```
60	
61	## The one rule to remember
62	
63	**If the objective is only partly advanced, set nothing.** The task returns to
64	`queued` and the next round continues it. Reserve `done` for work that is
65	completely finished — that is the entire point of the status now living with you
66	instead of being guessed from your report.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffPullIndep

/-!
# F5 — the `pull` field itself

`Picard/DivRepAffPullGlue.lean` glues the chart pulls of a *given* atlas factorization, and
`Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` shows the glued class does not depend on which factorization
was used.  This file takes the last step and *defines* the forward map:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsDivRepPullValue` — the characterizing property of the value: it
  restricts, over some atlas factorization of `v`, to the chart pull of every piece.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullValue` — **the `pull` field**, `Classical.choice` over the
  factorization supplied by `divScheme_exists_chartFactor`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullValue_spec` / `_eq_of` — it satisfies the property, and it is
  the *unique* class satisfying it.  `_eq_of` is what makes the definition usable: a caller
  who has *any* factorization of `v` and *any* class restricting to its chart pulls knows that
  class is `divRepPullValue v`, without ever unfolding the choice.

**Why the choice is harmless, and this is the whole point of the two previous files.** The
value is pinned by `IsDivRepPullValue` up to nothing at all: two classes with the property
have factorizations, possibly different ones, and
`divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors` equates them across the cross-refinement.  So
`divRepPullValue` is a function of `v` alone, and the `Classical.choice` never leaks into a
statement.

The remaining fields of `DivRepAffinePullback` are `isDivRepClassify_pull` (the ε-gated one)
and `pull_naturality`, whose carrier transport is `Picard/DivRepAwayPush.lean`.  As everywhere
in this layer, all of it is conditional on a supplied chart family `U` and its compatibility
`hU` — see the header of `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` for what that conditionality does and
does not buy.
-/
